title: News-Conditional Intraday Alpha: LLM Sentiment + LOB Microstructure vs. Loughran-McDonald Lexicon
primary_hypothesis: LLM sentiment scores on news headlines combined with LOBSTER OFI and depth thinning produces higher out-of-sample IC than Loughran-McDonald lexicon sentiment alone, across 10 large-cap S&P 500 names at 1/5/15 minute horizons.

observations.claim: LM sentiment on news headlines has high vocabulary miss-rate (~40-60% zero-signal events) due to calibration on 10-K filings, not short-form text.
LOBSTER OFI at 1-minute bars is positively correlated with contemporaneous and forward mid-quote returns for liquid large-cap NASDAQ names.
Depth thinning (withdrawal of resting limit orders) on the ask side precedes upward directional moves by 10-60 seconds.
LLM-class models (GPT-4o, FinBERT) achieve higher classification accuracy than LM on financial news sentiment benchmarks (FPB, FiQA SA).
observations.source: Lopez-Lira & Tang (2023); Koa et al. (2024) — citations unverified

explanations.claim: LM zero-signal events dilute rank IC by inflating ties at zero, biasing Spearman correlation toward zero.
LLMs capture negation, implicit sentiment, and domain-specific context that LM word lists miss, yielding higher signal-to-noise on headlines.
OFI is a revealed-preference signal from informed traders; it is mechanically predictive but uninformative about the cause of directional pressure.
Depth thinning reflects market-maker adverse selection concerns; it leads OFI by seconds and is therefore an earlier predictor of price moves.

exploitations.claim: A composite signal combining LLM sentiment, multi-level OFI, and depth thinning asymmetry achieves higher out-of-sample IC than LM-only at 1/5/15 min horizons.
exploitations.blocker: Phase 3 IC evaluation with DM test — not yet run

exploitations.claim: The interaction term (LLM sentiment direction × OFI sign agreement) carries incremental IC beyond the additive combination of the two signals.
exploitations.blocker: Phase 3 interaction regression — not yet designed

justifications.claim: Spearman IC is the appropriate evaluation metric: it is robust to heavy tails in intraday returns and standard in practitioner factor research (Grinold & Kahn).
Diebold-Mariano test is appropriate for comparing time-series IC sequences, accounting for autocorrelation via HAC standard errors.
Multi-level OFI dominates single-level (best bid/ask) OFI for return prediction at 1-5 minute horizons.
justifications.blocker: Xu et al. citation unverified — needs literature confirmation

bridges.gap: LLM superiority on sentiment benchmarks (daily/long-horizon) may not transfer to intraday (1-min) where microstructure noise dominates.
bridges.mitigation: Measure IC separately at each horizon; expect stronger LLM advantage at 5/15 min than 1 min.

bridges.gap: Depth thinning after news arrival may be a consequence of the price move rather than a predictor — reverse causality risk.
bridges.mitigation: Use only depth thinning measured strictly before the news timestamp (pre-announcement LOB state).

bridges.gap: 10 stocks is a small cross-section; IC estimates will have wide confidence intervals and DM test may be underpowered.
bridges.mitigation: Report per-stock IC with bootstrap CIs; frame as existence proof, not universal claim.

data_requirements.news_source: TBD — requires millisecond-precision timestamps (Refinitiv/LSEG, Bloomberg, Benzinga)

experiment_plan.description: Verify OFI formula implementation on 1-day LOBSTER sample for AAPL; check IC against mid-quote return.
Compute OFI and depth thinning features for all 10 names over 2022 Q1. Measure IC at 1/5/15 min. Baseline check.
Score 2022 Q1 news headlines with LM and FinBERT. Measure headline-level IC at 1/5/15 min. Compare LM vs FinBERT IC.
Full 2-year evaluation: composite signal IC vs LM-only IC. DM test at each horizon. Interaction term test.
Robustness: sub-sample by VIX regime, news category (earnings/macro/analyst/M&A), time of day.

convergence.primary_blocker: No experimental IC measurements yet — all exploitation claims are proposed or under_investigation
